text:
ConocoPhillips stock fell 3.3% today to $127.53, continuing a sharp slide over the past week as oil prices have whipsawed on conflicting signals about Iran tensions and Middle East supply. The stock has lost 5% in two weeks, reflecting broader volatility in energy markets: crude swung from below $100 a barrel on Monday (after Trump signaled willingness to negotiate with Iran) back up as Treasury Secretary Bessent announced Iranian airlines would be shut down starting Wednesday, then fell again as traders assessed that Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline closure would eventually ease supply constraints once it recovers.

The outsized move in the stock relative to the oil price direction suggests investors are pricing in real uncertainty about both near-term geopolitical risk and longer-term energy supply. With oil prices now split—U.S. crude at $107 versus world crude at $131—there's a wide disparity in what refinery margins (profit from converting crude to products) might be, which affects company fundamentals differently depending on where ConocoPhillips operates and what it produces.
